The verified inherited stack enforces both lists in _beforeTokenTransfer: mTokenPermissioned requires M_GLOBAL_GREENLISTED_ROLE on both from and to for non-mint/burn transfers, and mToken calls _onlyNotBlacklisted on both sides against BLACKLISTED_ROLE. The controlling roles have current members: hasRole(M_GLOBAL_GREENLISTED_ROLE 0x49a1…0acc, 0x0461bd693cae49be9d030e5c212e080f9c78b846)=true and hasRole(BLACKLIST_OPERATOR_ROLE 0x2fdc…89ff, 0x081bb8ad7f452f916991c17fdfa64d4a25153169)=true, while DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is held by 0xb60842e9dabcd1c52e354ac30e82a97661cb7e89 and 0xd4195cf4df289a4748c1a7b6ddbe770e27ba1227. Because the issuer/operator can de-list a greenlisted holder and can add any holder to the blacklist, reviewedStatus is true.

oracleRisk.summary: mGLOBAL is an issuer NAV-accreting tokenized certificate, not a market-priced asset. Midas documents the mToken NAV as strategy-manager-provided, internally reviewed and fee-adjusted by Midas, and co-signed by at least two Midas reviewers before it is pushed onchain to the mGLOBAL/USD Oracle Feed, where deviation bounds, heartbeat freshness, and hardcoded price limits gate its use by the issuance and redemption contracts. Third-party oracle networks (Chainlink, Pyth) are documented only for payment-token pricing; the certificate's own valuation authority is internal. This review classifies the documented fund-level pricing authority, not updater-key independence, signer collusion resistance, or downstream lending integrations that consume the feed.

branchApplicability.reviewer: RS-095 research sprint 2026-10-29 (Midas NAV pricing review)
branchApplicability.rationale: mGLOBAL represents a managed private-credit fund share whose mint and redemption pricing come from the issuer NAV. No borrower market liquidates against the token, so the fund-level NAV authority applies without oracle branches; lending markets that accept mGLOBAL are integrations, not the certificate's pricing mechanism.
